 SPORT Barbarez: We want to conclude the Year with a Victory against Romania
 Published: November 16, 2026 
 Share 
 ©️NS BiH 
 SHARE 
 The national team of Bosnia and Herzegovina will play its final match of the year tomorrow in Zenica. Head coach Sergej Barbarez anticipates a serious encounter against Romania and hopes the “Dragons” will gift the fans a good result. You can follow the match exclusively on BHRT broadcasts. The game is part of the Nations League.
 At a press conference, Barbarez stated that the team aims to maintain its current momentum, even though the match result will not alter their standing.
 “Every match is important—whether friendly or competitive—because each one contributes to the overall record, statistics, and the experience we still desperately need. That is how we view the match against Romania, even though the outcome changes nothing for us,” the head coach said.
 He expects a tough contest, emphasizing that nothing will be handed out for free.
 “Nothing will be given away by either side; we are in for a serious match. Naturally, we are pleased to play our final game at home, and we want to deliver a positive result for our fans,” Barbarez noted.
 He specifically addressed the health status of Haris Tabaković, who is dealing with a meniscus issue and will not be available to the team.
 “I believe he will be sidelined for the rest of the year. He is scheduled for surgery this week, and everything is proceeding as planned. I know this is difficult for him, and we will stand by him,” said Barbarez.
 Tarik Muharemović returns to the squad, having missed the previous match against Sweden due to a suspension. Reflecting on the 2–3 defeat—a match in which BiH trailed 0–3 at halftime—Muharemović praised the team’s response.
 “The way the guys fought back in the second half after being down 0–3 speaks to our hard work and our mentality. It’s not really appropriate to talk about what I might have done had I been playing. The lads fought, as they always do; whoever is in the squad knows how to play, possesses quality, and understands what needs to be done. Take the match against Qatar at the World Cup, for instance: I wasn’t there, yet we won—whereas in the first two matches, I played, and we didn’t win. So, everyone in the national team deserves to be here, and whoever the head coach selects, we know they will give 100 percent,” said Muharemović.
 Barbarez is satisfied with how the team responded following a poor first half against Sweden. Ahead of the match against Romania, he emphasized the importance of mental strength and a robust style of play.
 “We need to be strong, tough, and mentally prepared—playing with grit, just as we did in the second half against Sweden. That’s when we prove to ourselves that we can hold our own against very strong national teams. Our mentality has become one of our greatest strengths, and that pleases me,” said the head coach, adding that he is also pleased with the team’s tactical flexibility.
 Speaking about potential opponents in the play-offs, Muharemović mentioned that he would like to face Wales.
 “I have friends from Wales in Leeds, and they keep telling me they hope to play against BiH so they can get revenge for their previous defeat. That’s why I want to play them—it’s always fun when I return to the club and ask them how their trip to America went,” he said with a smile.
 In closing, Barbarez described the year as highly successful and expressed his desire for the national team to wrap it up with a positive result against Romania.
 “It has been a wonderful year, and I hope we can conclude it tomorrow with a good result. It all started with the play-offs, followed by advancing from the group stage at the World Cup, and now this Nations League campaign. Throughout all of this, we’ve proven that we have the power to determine our own destiny. I work with integrity, driven by a single goal for this national team and this country. That is my greatest victory,” concluded the head coach of the “Dragons.”
